question.problem:
The function $p(x)$ is continuous over $x\in [-6,5].$ Some values of $p(x)$ are given in the table below. 

| $x$ | $-6$ | $-2$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $p(x)$ | $4$ | $-1$ | $-3$ |

What is the smallest possible number of solutions to the equation $p(x)=2?$

The equation $p(x)=2$ has at least {{field-1}} solutions.
question.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a continuous function on $[-6,5],$ we can apply the Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT) in each subinterval of $[-6,5].$

We will go through each subinterval of $[-6,5]$ and check if the IVT guarantees a solution to the equation $p(x)=2$ on this interval.

- On the subinterval $[-6,-2],$ we have $p(-6)=4$ and $p(-2)=-1.$ Since $2\in [-1,4],$ the IVT *does* guarantee a solution to the equation $p(x)=2$ on this subinterval.

- On the subinterval $[-2,5],$ we have $p(-2)=-1$ and $p(5)=-3.$ Since $2\notin [-3,-1],$ the IVT does *not* guarantee a solution to the equation $p(x)=2$ on this subinterval.

The IVT guarantees solutions to $p(x)=2$ on $[-6,-2].$  

Therefore, $p(x)=2$ has at least $1$ solutions.
